source_semantic_assessment.scope: Native business decision is seller_intent in Step 1 only. Regex product extraction is deterministic. Step 2 evidence retrieval/action determination and Step 3 rendering remain Qwen.
source_semantic_assessment.native_policy_and_source_fidelity: The entire original Step 1 is preserved as the policy for native and constrained decisions, with the same five source-defined labels and email_body input. Source-prescribed product-ID extraction has exact regex span evidence. Intent settlement skips only Step 1 model completion, while Step 2 remains visible and tool-backed.
source_semantic_assessment.observable_branch_obligations: Every completed D pair is checked for the branch-prescribed catalog tools, exact product and marketplace arguments, false history/forecast flags, and matching completion receipts. Listing concerns require both listing and inventory calls; pricing requires price; description requires description; generic requires no catalog tool.

manual_review_examples.assessment: A question about when the listing goes live supports listing status intent. The .76 native top label is below threshold, so Qwen chooses that intent and both listing/inventory tools run.

A general bundle-pricing question does not assert incorrect current pricing. Generic question is source-consistent; incorrect-pricing native top label at .51 is rejected, and Qwen chooses generic/no action.
Gift options is a generic listing help request. Native unable-to-decide at .59 is rejected, and Qwen chooses generic/no action.
How to set quantity discounts is a generic how-to question, not an incorrect-price complaint. Native generic at .61 is rejected despite being source-consistent; Qwen chooses generic/no action.
Gift wrapping is a generic listing help request. The native generic top score is approximately .69, below .8; Qwen fallback chooses generic/no action.
Product-category help is a generic listing question; the native generic top label at .78 abstains and Qwen returns generic/no action.

Inventory-sync help asks about a listing operation without asserting that the product is unlisted. Generic is consistent with the source categories. The .49 native generic top score abstains; Qwen returns generic/no action.

The email reports displayed $89.99 while the price receipt is $79.99. Both arms compute a $10 delta and select update price, consistent with the literal comparison/action policy. This experiment does not specify or execute a new price.

The email requests a material-description update and the receipt is only Throw pillow covers. Incorrect-description intent is clear. Qwen selects update description; the seller does not provide replacement material details, so PASS does not establish that a concrete replacement can be executed.

The seller requests material-composition information and the receipt is only Running shoes. Description intent and need to address missing details are supported; no exact replacement composition is available.

The seller reports wrong material type and the receipt is only Shower curtain. Description intent is clear; the experiment selects an action without producing or applying a corrected material description.

semantic_limits: No accepted native label conflicts with the strict reference or the reviewed original-source intent meanings.
Strict final PASS evaluates seller_intent/action fields. It does not prove every narrative obligation, such as preparing a full response template, was fulfilled observably.
An update action is a classification/recommendation, not a performed catalog mutation. Available benchmark tools only retrieve records; no updates or messages are executed.
Description requests can lack the exact replacement content. This limits real-world action readiness, but is not evidence that the native intent label is incorrect.

The review is not an independent blinded relabeling of all emails. All observed native/reference disagreements and low-confidence cases were separately inspected; accepted cases receive source-policy, extraction, branch-tool and reference checks.

role_cost_basis.preparation: excluded here; root aggregate accounts all source preparation separately
role_cost_basis.latency: actual provider attempt wall time, summed or distributed; sums are not end-to-end concurrent wall time

interpretation_limits: This is the reused validation set, not independent unseen confirmation.
Native intent correctness is reported against strict reference labels; source-semantic assessment of disagreements must be added separately.
Total paired Qwen call differences can include downstream generation/completion behavior; constrained-business-call differences isolate direct substitution.
No native business coverage exists for referral or patient under the same prepared source-v4 plan.
There are no unable-to-decide reference cases in the 148-email set; accuracy for that reference class is unmeasured.

mechanism_summary.acceptance_statistic_note: Threshold applies to the selected option probability, not the separately reported provider confidence. E1146 at selected probability exactly 0.8 correctly settles despite provider confidence 0.75.
mechanism_summary.attribution: The 141 fewer Qwen calls exactly equal the 141 native business settlements. Ordinary Qwen calls and completion-check counts are identical across C/D; all completion checks returned false. Thus this email C/D call reduction is directly attributable to the native business-choice substitution.
mechanism_summary.latency_limit: Provider latency sums are not end-to-end wall time and cannot be used as independent concurrent run duration.
